analysis:
This batch is documentation only: the changelog, provider.md (head 76-89) and hardware-support.md (head 318-340). No Swift source was supplied, so every behavior claim below is unverified.

1) Prompt token reuse (PromptTokenCache.swift, PromptPieceTokenStore). Template pieces are cached per prefix-cache scope in ordinary heap, bounded by DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE_MB (default 32 MiB per tokenizer). This is new retention of A-001-derived data and a new TTFT oracle. It is flagged as a threat-model gap under T-041/T-028.
   Integration must verify:
   - the scope key is the coordinator cacheSalt (T-041 mitigation), not a model-only or caller-controlled key;
   - the store is cleared on unload;
   - mismatch self-checks fail closed to the old tokenization path.

2) Linear-time template rewrites for Gemma 4 and GPT-OSS (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_TEMPLATE_LOOPS). Divergence from the served template could change the prompt contract identity or tokens. Load-time and sampled background checks are claimed but unverified (T-007/T-056 adjacent).

3) Single-parse request body. The extension-field parse must not differ from the chat-request parse for requests without tools.

4) Cold-load FIFO release (ProviderLoop+WorkFIFO.swift releaseWorkFIFO/awaitReleasedLoads, fastAdmissionReject).
   - Lets cancels and attestation challenges proceed during a load, which helps availability (T-057/TB-011).
   - Integration must check that a cancel for the waiting request is still applied after admission returns (T-010).
   - It must also check that App Attest grants and connection invalidation still revoke a request accepted before the change while its load completes (T-053).
   - The docs acknowledge that an accepted load can fail after acceptance when a resident model keeps its slot. This is availability only.
   - The pending-load claims and the memory gate are said to remain authoritative.

New env knobs need passthroughEnvKeys review for the installed daemon.

findings.detail: The changelog (lines 3-11) and hardware-support.md (head 332-337) add `PromptPieceTokenStore`, which keeps token IDs for chat-template pieces between requests. It is keyed by prefix-cache scope and holds up to 32 MiB per loaded tokenizer. This retains A-001-derived plaintext in process heap after a request finishes. T-028 covers residual GPU/KV memory and T-041 covers the SSD prefix tier, but neither covers this store. It also adds a second hit/miss timing signal: changelog line 9 cites 5-8 ms versus 102-264 ms preparation. If the scope key is the coordinator-authored cacheSalt, this stays inside the same-account exposure SEC-035 already accepts. If it uses a weaker key, such as model only or a caller-supplied field, it becomes a cross-tenant prefix-confirmation oracle. Trigger: a consumer replays a guessed conversation prefix and measures TTFT. Impact: confirms another tenant's prompt content. Fix: key the store strictly on the authenticated cacheSalt/scope, never caller fields. Clear it on model unload and KEK/cache wipe. Record it under T-041/T-028 with its lifetime, its bound and the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0 kill switch.
findings.title: New cross-request in-memory store of prompt-derived token pieces is not in the threat model
